guide_passage: Moved here by the author's ruling, from Make the Protector Visible: "Leave a relationship that keeps eroding safety." And from this section's third guide paragraph, the one sentence the article hadn't carried yet: "And you do not need repeated exposure to danger before protecting yourself."
next: Notice your side too. Feeling guilty does not prove that you did something wrong; it also does not prove that somebody manipulated you. Did you cause harm that needs repair, or are you abandoning your position to make their disappointment go away? Sometimes both are present.
rulings:
Joel, 2026-09-29, on P3: "you were conflating protection from nurturing (giving a meal is nurturing, throwing away moldy food is protection, and we already have that in P1). So I threw away the duplicated examples of protection."
Joel, 2026-09-29, on P1's self-love sentence: "lack of self love isn't the only reason to stay in an unsafe relationship, but it is the underlying reason. if you lack self love, all the others will follow: uncertainty about your goals, lack of skill follows that uncertainty, exhaustion follows that uncertainty and the lack of skill, practical barriers are less actual barriers when the goal is understood to be self love"
Joel, 2026-09-29, on logic: "the logic should be grounded in the meaning the reader needs to understand" (a flat "shows" where the guide says "can be" was pedantic to flag).
Joel, 2026-09-29, on P3: "line it up better with the guide" (one guide paragraph's job per paragraph; this paragraph is the first half of guide paragraph 4, split at its natural break because Joel breaks paragraphs at two beats).
Joel, 2026-09-30, rethinking P1's relationship line from his own experience: someone can feel less and less safe with a partner, and at other times see that their own mind was playing tricks on them; lack of self-love was behind it, and it had nothing to do with the partner. "So now the advice to leave the relationship becomes more tricky with that in mind... it just depends on how things were going for [them] at the time." His wording, instead of "leave it" and the self-love reason: "meditate on why it makes you feel unsafe, and what keeps you in it, and whether either may be due to a lack of the healed inner child/inner adult relationship."
Joel, 2026-09-30, on his Substack note (embedded as a card in Also Look Outward): "it reads also more human and captivating when it's a back-and-forth discussion with other substackers rather than just the narrative voice all the time."
Joel, 2026-09-30 04:44, on scope: "in general we should assume the user doesn't want to massively increase the article size, but small increases or decreases may be fine if warranted. for any uncertainty ask the user."
